subject: Post-call recap + burst provisioning qualification for Cliffside.ai
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Reed <jordan.reed@cliffside.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 20 Dec 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call recap + burst provisioning qualification for Cliffside.ai

Jordan — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and the plan we discussed so you have a single reference: 

Key takeaways / pain points
- Primary pain: unpredictable burst traffic from marketing campaigns (~6x baseline for short windows) causes high tail latency and heavy billing spikes.
- Current infra: self-hosted endpoints on a small GPU pool with ~120 rps steady-state, spikes to 650 rps for 2–10 minute bursts.
- Latency targets: 95th percentile must stay under 150 ms for 32-token completions during peak campaigns.
- Cost sensitivity: want predictable monthly spend, with a hard cap option for campaign windows.
- Compliance: need confirmation on audit logs retention (90 days) and KMS integration for model artifacts.

What we propose (summary)
- Burst provisioning model: dedicated baseline pool + short-lived burst capacity that can scale to ~6x within 90s using pre-warmed instances and fast cold-start mitigations.
- Topology: multi-variant routing: primary low-latency model (quantized 8-bit) for most traffic + cheaper compatible variant as fallback during sustained overload.
- Autoscale controls: concurrency-based autoscale + manual burst grants for scheduled campaigns.

Next steps we agreed
1) We (Redwood) will send a short capacity simulation and an initial topology sketch. (attached: initial-call-notes.pdf, capacity-model-v1.xlsx)
2) You to share recent sample traffic traces (1 week preferred) and a couple of representative payload sizes (~tokens per request).
3) Technical deep-dive follow-up with Grace (infrastructure) to validate cold-start windows and KV-cache behavior — propose Tue or Wed next week.
4) High-level pricing envelope for burst windows and a managed cap option.

For clarity on SLOs we heard today: 95th < 150ms during burst (32 tokens), 99th < 400ms, sustained throughput > 400 rps without error rate increase. If any of those numbers are off, tell us and we’ll adjust.

Attachments included: initial-call-notes.pdf, capacity-model-v1.xlsx (lightweight model).

If that all looks good I’ll lock a 30-minute slot for the deep-dive with Grace.

Thanks —
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0186

Thanks, Karthik — this is very helpful. A couple clarifications from our side: 

- The 6x spikes are accurate but usually come as a sharp 2–5 minute window right after email blasts. Occasionally they have a longer tail of 10–12 minutes.
- We currently see error rate climb when the queue reaches ~1.2s request wait, so minimizing queueing is critical.
- Our payloads vary: conversational agents avg ~48 tokens in/out; webhook-style requests can be 8–16 tokens.
- Compliance: 90-day audit logs are fine but we need explicit confirmation that KMS keys used for model artifacts can be customer-managed (we have FedRAMP constraints for some clients).

Two asks before the deep-dive: 
1) Can you share a very rough cost delta for a one-off 6x burst for 10 minutes vs sustaining extra baseline for the month? Even a ballpark helps.
2) If you can simulate cold-start behavior for our baseline+burst topology (how long to reach steady throughput) that would be great.

If Tue/ Wed works for Grace, I’ll book Tuesday 11am PT.

— Jordan

Subject: Re: Post-call recap + burst provisioning qualification for Cliffside.ai

Jordan — hi, Grace from Redwood infra here. I pulled together a short technical runbook and a small simulation attached (burst-capacity-simulation.csv, redwood-topology-draft.drawio.pdf). Key notes below.

Technical deep-dive (summary)
- Model choice and quantization: recommend a quantized 1-2 variant approach: primary: 34B quantized (8-bit) for low-latency; fallback: 70% cheaper compatible variant for degraded mode. Both variants should share KV-cache warm paths where possible to reduce cold-start overhead.
- Cold-start and pre-warm: warm start using cached KV and pre-warmed containers reduces median cold-start to ~18s and P95 cold-start to ~45s in our sim (numbers depend on model binary size and host GPU memory). Pre-warm strategy: staggered pre-warm based on campaign schedule + quick scale replicas for unexpected spikes.
- Autoscale policy: concurrency-based scaling with rapid scale-up (target 90s to 6x) using a combination of vertical concurrency (more requests per replica) and horizontal burst nodes. We avoid single large scale events; smaller parallel replicas reduce queueing.
- Cache & batching: enable prefix KV-cache for conversational flows — observed 30–40% token compute reduction for repeated prompts. Continuous batching window tuned to 5–10ms for lowest incremental latency.
- Networking: prioritize colocated load balancing for campaign endpoints to avoid cross-zone throttling; recommend regional routing for US-west and failover to us-east if capacity constrained.

SLO mapping (what we can realistically commit to for testing)
- P95 latency for 32-token responses: target < 150 ms under burst with pre-warm; without pre-warm expect P95 ~220–350 ms depending on burst ramp.
- Sustained throughput: confirmed ability to sustain > 400 rps on a dedicated pool sized per our capacity model.
- Error budgets: short burst windows (<=10 minutes) can be covered by temporary capacity buffers — we propose an error budget policy that triggers fallback to cheaper variant at 5xx thresholds.

Attachments included: burst-capacity-simulation.csv (synthetic traffic runs), redwood-topology-draft.drawio.pdf (topology sketch). I also updated capacity-model-v1.xlsx with the note about pre-warm requirements; sending that to you now.

Questions for Cliffside before we size the final pool
- Can you share 1 week of request timestamps (anonymized) and breakdown by payload size (tokens)?
- Any strict no-fallback constraints? If you require 100% fidelity we can't use the cheap fallback variant.
- Are scheduled campaigns predictable (so we can pre-warm) or always ad-hoc?

Proposed next steps
- You share traces -> we run 2 simulations (safety + performance) and return a recommended baseline pool size + burst configuration.
- Schedule a 45-minute deep-dive (Grace + Karthik + Cliffside infra) — Jordan suggested Tue 11am PT, works for me.

I added some inline numbers in the attached simulation to give a cost delta example. High-level: a 10-minute 6x burst priced as an on-demand burst is typically 25–40% cheaper than keeping that extra baseline for a month (depends on utilization). We can produce an exact estimate once we have traces.

Thanks —
Grace O'Connor
Principal Infrastructure Engineer | Redwood Inference
